title: Moby-Dick
author: Herman Melville
summary: Novel, 1851. Ishmael, the narrator, signs on to the whaler Pequod out of Nantucket with his friend Queequeg, a harpooneer. Captain Ahab, who lost a leg to the white sperm whale Moby Dick, reveals that the voyage is a hunt for revenge and nails a gold doubloon to the mast as a reward for the first man to sight the whale. First mate Starbuck objects; the other mates are Stubb and Flask, the harpooneers Queequeg, Tashtego and Daggoo. After a three-day chase Moby Dick rams and sinks the Pequod; Ahab is caught by his own harpoon line and dragged under. Ishmael alone survives, floating on Queequeg's coffin, and is picked up by the whaler Rachel.

title: Pride and Prejudice
author: Jane Austen
summary: Novel, 1813. The Bennets have five daughters and an estate entailed to their cousin Mr Collins. Wealthy Mr Bingley falls for the eldest, Jane; his proud friend Mr Darcy offends Elizabeth. The charming officer Wickham tells Elizabeth lies about Darcy. Darcy's first proposal, at Hunsford, is refused; his letter then explains Wickham's past and his own part in separating Bingley and Jane. When the youngest sister, Lydia, runs off with Wickham, Darcy secretly pays for their marriage. Lady Catherine de Bourgh tries to stop the match; Darcy proposes again and Elizabeth accepts. Jane marries Bingley.

title: A Tale of Two Cities
author: Charles Dickens
summary: Novel, 1859, set in London and Paris before and during the French Revolution. Dr Manette is freed after eighteen years in the Bastille and reunited with his daughter Lucie. Charles Darnay, nephew of the cruel Marquis St. Evremonde, renounces his title and marries Lucie. Sydney Carton, a dissolute English lawyer who looks almost exactly like Darnay, also loves her. During the Revolution Darnay goes to Paris to help a servant, is arrested and, denounced by the Defarges using a letter Manette wrote in prison, sentenced to death. Carton drugs Darnay, takes his place and goes to the guillotine: 'It is a far, far better thing that I do, than I have ever done.' Darnay, Lucie and their child escape to England; Madame Defarge is killed in a struggle with Miss Pross.

title: Treasure Island
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
summary: Novel, 1883. Jim Hawkins helps run the Admiral Benbow inn. An old pirate, Billy Bones, dies there, and Jim finds Captain Flint's treasure map in his sea chest. Squire Trelawney and Dr Livesey fit out the schooner Hispaniola under Captain Smollett; the one-legged ship's cook, Long John Silver, fills the crew with former pirates. Hiding in an apple barrel, Jim overhears their plan to mutiny. On the island the loyal party holds a stockade; Jim meets the marooned Ben Gunn, who has already dug up the treasure and hidden it in his cave. Jim cuts the ship adrift and kills the pirate Israel Hands. Silver changes sides to save himself; the treasure is loaded and they sail home, and Silver slips away at a port with a bag of coins.

title: The Three Musketeers
author: Alexandre Dumas
summary: Novel, 1844. In 1625 young d'Artagnan comes from Gascony to Paris to join the King's Musketeers and befriends the three musketeers, Athos, Porthos and Aramis, after challenging each of them to a duel. D'Artagnan is not one of the three; he is the fourth friend. They oppose Cardinal Richelieu and his agents, the Comte de Rochefort and Milady de Winter, and recover the Queen's diamond studs from the Duke of Buckingham in England. Milady, who turns out to be Athos's branded former wife, poisons d'Artagnan's love Constance Bonacieux and arranges Buckingham's murder. The friends capture and execute her, and Richelieu gives d'Artagnan a lieutenant's commission.

title: Frankenstein
author: Mary Shelley
summary: Novel, 1818, told through Captain Walton's letters from the Arctic. Victor Frankenstein, a student at Ingolstadt, builds a creature from parts taken from charnel houses and dissecting rooms and brings it to life, then flees in horror. The creature, rejected everywhere, learns to speak and read by secretly watching the De Lacey family. It kills Victor's young brother William, and the servant Justine is hanged for it. It demands a mate; Victor starts one and destroys it. The creature then kills Victor's friend Clerval and his bride Elizabeth on their wedding night. Victor pursues it into the Arctic and dies on Walton's ship; the creature mourns him and goes off to die.

title: Dracula
author: Bram Stoker
summary: Novel, 1897, told in diaries and letters. Solicitor Jonathan Harker visits Count Dracula in Transylvania and becomes his prisoner. Dracula sails to Whitby, England, and preys on Lucy Westenra, who dies and rises as a vampire; Professor Van Helsing, her fiance Arthur Holmwood, Dr Seward and Quincey Morris destroy her. Dracula then attacks Harker's wife, Mina. The men sterilise his boxes of earth and chase him back to Transylvania, where Harker and Morris kill him at sunset; Morris dies of his wounds.

title: Jane Eyre
author: Charlotte Bronte
summary: Novel, 1847. The orphan Jane is mistreated by her aunt Mrs Reed and sent to the harsh Lowood school, where her friend Helen Burns dies. As governess at Thornfield Hall she falls in love with its master, Mr Rochester, but their wedding is stopped: he already has a wife, Bertha Mason, insane and locked in the attic. Jane flees, is taken in by the Rivers siblings, who prove to be her cousins, inherits money from an uncle, and refuses St John Rivers's proposal. Hearing Rochester call her, she returns to find Thornfield burned, Bertha dead, and Rochester blind and missing a hand. 'Reader, I married him.'

title: Wuthering Heights
author: Emily Bronte
summary: Novel, 1847, told by the tenant Lockwood and the housekeeper Nelly Dean. Mr Earnshaw brings home the foundling Heathcliff, who grows up devoted to Catherine Earnshaw and abused by her brother Hindley. Catherine marries Edgar Linton instead; Heathcliff leaves, returns rich, marries Edgar's sister Isabella out of spite and takes Wuthering Heights from the drunken Hindley. Catherine dies giving birth to a daughter, Cathy. Heathcliff forces Cathy to marry his sickly son Linton to gain the Linton estate. After Linton dies, Heathcliff loses interest in revenge and dies, and Cathy and Hindley's son Hareton fall in love.

title: Great Expectations
author: Charles Dickens
summary: Novel, 1861. The orphan Pip, raised by his sister and the blacksmith Joe Gargery, helps an escaped convict, Magwitch, on the marshes. He is sent to play at the house of the jilted Miss Havisham and falls for her cold ward Estella. An unknown benefactor makes Pip a gentleman in London; he assumes it is Miss Havisham, but it is Magwitch, who returns illegally from Australia. Pip tries to smuggle him abroad; Magwitch is caught and dies. Miss Havisham is fatally burned. Estella, who is Magwitch's daughter, marries the brutal Bentley Drummle. Years later Pip meets the widowed Estella in the ruins of Satis House, and the book ends with the hope that they will not part.

title: Oliver Twist
author: Charles Dickens
summary: Novel, 1838. The workhouse orphan Oliver asks for more gruel, is apprenticed to an undertaker, and runs away to London, where the Artful Dodger brings him to Fagin's gang of child thieves. The kindly Mr Brownlow takes him in, but Nancy and Bill Sikes drag him back. His half-brother Monks plots to ruin him. Nancy warns Rose Maylie and is murdered by Sikes, who dies while fleeing. Fagin is hanged. Oliver is adopted by Mr Brownlow, and Rose turns out to be his aunt.

title: David Copperfield
author: Charles Dickens
summary: Novel, 1850. David's cruel stepfather, Mr Murdstone, sends him to work in a London bottling warehouse, where he lodges with the hopeful, penniless Mr Micawber. He runs to his aunt Betsey Trotwood in Dover, who raises him. His charming friend Steerforth seduces Little Em'ly; Steerforth and Ham later drown in a storm. David marries the childlike Dora, who dies young. Micawber exposes the clerk Uriah Heep's fraud against Mr Wickfield. David becomes a successful writer and marries Agnes Wickfield.

title: A Christmas Carol
author: Charles Dickens
summary: Novella, 1843. The miser Ebenezer Scrooge is visited on Christmas Eve by the ghost of his partner Jacob Marley and then by the Ghosts of Christmas Past, Present and Yet to Come. He sees his lost youth, his clerk Bob Cratchit's poor family and sick son Tiny Tim, and finally his own unmourned grave. He wakes on Christmas morning a changed man, sends the Cratchits a prize turkey, raises Bob's wages, and becomes a second father to Tiny Tim, who does not die.

title: Adventures of Huckleberry Finn
author: Mark Twain
summary: Novel, 1884. Huck escapes his drunken father by faking his own death and rafts down the Mississippi with Jim, who has run away from Miss Watson to avoid being sold. They drift through a family feud and fall in with two con men, the duke and the king, who sell Jim. Huck decides he would rather 'go to hell' than betray Jim and sets out to free him from the Phelps farm, where Tom Sawyer arrives and stages an absurdly elaborate escape; Tom is shot in the leg. Tom then reveals that Miss Watson died and freed Jim in her will. Huck's father is dead, and Huck plans to 'light out for the Territory.'

title: The Adventures of Tom Sawyer
author: Mark Twain
summary: Novel, 1876, set in St. Petersburg on the Mississippi. Tom tricks his friends into whitewashing Aunt Polly's fence and courts Becky Thatcher. In the graveyard at midnight he and Huck Finn see Injun Joe murder Dr Robinson; the drunk Muff Potter is blamed, and Tom testifies to save him. Tom, Huck and Joe Harper run off to Jackson's Island and come back in time for their own funeral. Tom and Becky get lost in McDougal's Cave, where Tom sees Injun Joe; after they escape the cave is sealed and Joe dies inside. Tom and Huck find the robbers' gold, twelve thousand dollars.

title: The Hound of the Baskervilles
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
summary: Sherlock Holmes novel, 1902. Sir Charles Baskerville is found dead on Dartmoor beside the footprints of a gigantic hound, as in an old family legend. Holmes sends Dr Watson to guard the heir, Sir Henry. An escaped convict on the moor turns out to be the butler's wife's brother. The real villain is the naturalist Stapleton, secretly a Baskerville heir, who uses a huge dog daubed with phosphorus. Holmes uses Sir Henry as bait, the hound is shot, and Stapleton flees into the Grimpen Mire and is presumed drowned.

title: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
summary: Sherlock Holmes is Arthur Conan Doyle's consulting detective at 221B Baker Street, London, told by his friend Dr John Watson. He first appears in the novel A Study in Scarlet (1887). The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes (1892) collects twelve stories, including A Scandal in Bohemia, where Irene Adler outwits him; The Red-Headed League, a bank tunnel disguised as a job; and The Speckled Band, a murder by a trained snake. His enemy Professor Moriarty appears in The Final Problem, where Holmes seems to die at the Reichenbach Falls before returning in later stories.

title: The Count of Monte Cristo
author: Alexandre Dumas
summary: Novel, 1844. The young sailor Edmond Dantes is framed as a Bonapartist agent by the jealous Danglars and Fernand, who wants his fiancee Mercedes, and the prosecutor Villefort buries the evidence to protect himself. Dantes spends fourteen years in the Chateau d'If, where the Abbe Faria educates him and tells him of a treasure on the island of Monte Cristo. He escapes in Faria's burial sack, finds the treasure, and returns as the Count of Monte Cristo. He exposes Fernand's treason, and Fernand shoots himself; Villefort goes mad after his wife poisons members of the family and herself; Danglars is ruined but spared. Dantes rewards the Morrel family and sails away with Haydee: 'wait and hope.'

title: Les Miserables
author: Victor Hugo
summary: Novel, 1862. Jean Valjean, released after nineteen years in prison for stealing bread, is shown mercy by Bishop Myriel, who gives him silver candlesticks. Under a new name he becomes a factory owner and mayor, and promises the dying Fantine to care for her daughter Cosette, whom he rescues from the greedy Thenardiers. Inspector Javert hunts him for years. In Paris, Cosette falls in love with the student Marius, who fights at the barricades in the 1832 uprising. Valjean carries the wounded Marius through the sewers and spares Javert's life; Javert, unable to reconcile mercy with law, drowns himself in the Seine. Marius and Cosette marry, and Valjean dies with them at his side.

title: Don Quixote
author: Miguel de Cervantes
summary: Novel in two parts, 1605 and 1615. Alonso Quixano, a Spanish gentleman, reads so many chivalric romances that he becomes the knight-errant Don Quixote, rides out on his old horse Rocinante with the peasant Sancho Panza as squire, and devotes himself to the imaginary lady Dulcinea. He attacks windmills he believes are giants and sheep he takes for armies. In the second part a duke and duchess play elaborate jokes on him and make Sancho governor of an 'island'. Defeated by the Knight of the White Moon, his neighbour Samson Carrasco in disguise, he goes home, recovers his sanity, renounces chivalry and dies.

title: War and Peace
author: Leo Tolstoy
summary: Novel, 1869, following Russian families through the Napoleonic wars from 1805 to 1812. Pierre Bezukhov inherits a fortune and makes an unhappy marriage to Helene. Prince Andrei Bolkonsky is wounded at Austerlitz and later engaged to young Natasha Rostova, who nearly elopes with the rake Anatole Kuragin. Napoleon invades in 1812; after Borodino, Moscow burns. Andrei is mortally wounded and dies after reconciling with Natasha. Pierre is taken prisoner and finds peace through the peasant Platon Karataev. Helene dies; Pierre marries Natasha, and Nikolai Rostov marries Andrei's sister Marya.

title: Anna Karenina
author: Leo Tolstoy
summary: Novel, 1878. Anna, married to the cold official Karenin, falls in love with the cavalry officer Count Vronsky, has his child and leaves her husband, losing her son and her place in society. Isolated and consumed by jealousy, she throws herself under a train. A parallel story follows the landowner Levin, his marriage to Kitty Shcherbatskaya, his work on the land, and his search for faith.

title: Crime and Punishment
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
summary: Novel, 1866. Raskolnikov, a poor former student in St. Petersburg, murders an old pawnbroker with an axe, telling himself that extraordinary men may break the law, and kills her sister Lizaveta when she walks in. Wracked by fever and guilt, he is circled by the detective Porfiry Petrovich. Sonya Marmeladova, forced into prostitution to feed her family, reads him the story of Lazarus. He confesses and is sentenced to eight years in Siberia; Sonya follows him, and the book ends with his first hope of renewal.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
summary: Novel, 1880. The dissolute Fyodor Karamazov has three sons, the passionate Dmitri, the intellectual Ivan and the gentle novice monk Alyosha, and probably a fourth, the servant Smerdyakov. Dmitri and his father compete for Grushenka. When Fyodor is murdered, Dmitri is tried and convicted. The killer is Smerdyakov, who took Ivan's idea that 'everything is permitted' as licence; he hangs himself before the trial, and Ivan collapses into fever. The book ends with Alyosha speaking to a group of boys at the funeral of young Ilyusha.

title: The Time Machine
author: H. G. Wells
summary: Novella, 1895. A Victorian inventor, the Time Traveller, tells his dinner guests of his journey to the year 802,701. Humanity has split into the gentle, childlike Eloi above ground and the underground Morlocks, who feed on them. He befriends an Eloi woman, Weena, loses his machine to the Morlocks and wins it back from inside the White Sphinx. Travelling on, he sees a dying Earth under a red sun millions of years later. He returns, tells the story, and leaves again, never to return.

title: The War of the Worlds
author: H. G. Wells
summary: Novel, 1898. Cylinders from Mars land on Horsell Common in Surrey. The Martians emerge in towering tripod machines armed with a heat-ray and poisonous black smoke and crush the army. The narrator flees, is trapped for days in a ruined house with a curate who breaks down, and finds London abandoned. The Martians are finally killed not by people but by earthly bacteria to which they have no immunity.

title: Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea
author: Jules Verne
summary: Novel, 1870. Professor Aronnax, his servant Conseil and the harpooner Ned Land join a hunt for a sea monster that is really Captain Nemo's submarine, the Nautilus. Nemo keeps them as prisoners on a voyage around the world under the sea: the ruins of Atlantis, the South Pole, a battle with giant squid. Nemo, a bitter enemy of the nations above, sinks a warship. As the Nautilus is caught in the Maelstrom off Norway, the three escape in a small boat.

title: Around the World in Eighty Days
author: Jules Verne
aliases: around the world in eighty days
summary: Novel, 1872. Phileas Fogg bets his Reform Club friends twenty thousand pounds that he can circle the globe in eighty days, and sets off with his French servant Passepartout. Detective Fix follows, believing Fogg is a bank robber. In India they rescue a young widow, Aouda, from being burned on her husband's funeral pyre. Fix arrests Fogg in Liverpool and he reaches London apparently five minutes late, but discovers that travelling east has gained him a day. He wins the bet and marries Aouda.

title: Alice's Adventures in Wonderland
author: Lewis Carroll
summary: Novel, 1865. Alice follows the White Rabbit down a rabbit hole and shrinks and grows by eating and drinking. She meets the Caterpillar, the Duchess and the grinning Cheshire Cat, joins the Mad Hatter's tea party with the March Hare and the Dormouse, and plays croquet with flamingos for the Queen of Hearts, who shouts 'Off with their heads!' At the trial of the Knave of Hearts, Alice grows to full size, defies the court, and wakes on the riverbank: it was a dream.

title: The Wonderful Wizard of Oz
author: L. Frank Baum
summary: Novel, 1900. A cyclone carries Dorothy's Kansas house to the Land of Oz, where it kills the Wicked Witch of the East; Dorothy takes her silver shoes. Following the yellow brick road to the Emerald City with the Scarecrow, who wants brains, the Tin Woodman, who wants a heart, and the Cowardly Lion, who wants courage, she is told by the Wizard to kill the Wicked Witch of the West, and melts her with a bucket of water. The Wizard turns out to be an ordinary man from Omaha; his balloon leaves without her. Glinda the Good Witch tells her the silver shoes can take her home, and they do.

title: Peter Pan
author: J. M. Barrie
summary: Novel, 1911 (Peter and Wendy), from the 1904 play. Peter Pan, the boy who will not grow up, teaches Wendy, John and Michael Darling to fly and takes them to Neverland, where they live with the Lost Boys and the fairy Tinker Bell. Captain Hook, whose hand was eaten by a crocodile that swallowed a clock, captures the children; Peter defeats him and Hook falls to the crocodile. The children go home, the Lost Boys are adopted by the Darlings, and Peter stays a boy, returning years later for Wendy's daughter Jane.

title: Little Women
author: Louisa May Alcott
summary: Novel, 1868-69. The four March sisters, sensible Meg, tomboy writer Jo, shy Beth and artistic Amy, grow up in New England with their mother Marmee while their father serves in the Civil War. They befriend the rich boy next door, Laurie. Meg marries the tutor John Brooke. Jo refuses Laurie's proposal and goes to New York to write. Beth, weakened by scarlet fever, dies. Amy marries Laurie in Europe, and Jo marries Professor Bhaer and opens a school at Plumfield.

title: Anne of Green Gables
author: Lucy Maud Montgomery
summary: Novel, 1908. Elderly siblings Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert of Avonlea, Prince Edward Island, send for an orphan boy to help on the farm and get red-haired, talkative Anne Shirley. Anne wins them over, finds a bosom friend in Diana Barry, and breaks her slate over Gilbert Blythe's head when he calls her 'Carrots', starting a long rivalry. She wins a scholarship at Queen's Academy, but after Matthew dies she gives it up to stay with Marilla. Gilbert gives her his post at the Avonlea school, and they become friends.

title: The Secret Garden
author: Frances Hodgson Burnett
summary: Novel, 1911. Mary Lennox, spoiled and orphaned by cholera in India, is sent to her uncle Archibald Craven's gloomy Misselthwaite Manor in Yorkshire. She finds the key to a walled garden locked since her aunt's death and restores it with the moorland boy Dickon. She discovers her hidden, bedridden cousin Colin, and the garden brings him health. Mr Craven returns to find his son running across the lawn.

title: The Wind in the Willows
author: Kenneth Grahame
summary: Novel, 1908. Mole leaves spring-cleaning to live by the river with Water Rat, and they befriend the wise Badger and the rich, boastful Mr Toad of Toad Hall. Toad's craze for motor cars lands him in prison; he escapes disguised as a washerwoman. While he is gone, weasels and stoats seize Toad Hall. Badger, Rat, Mole and Toad retake it through a secret tunnel, and Toad promises to reform.

title: The Jungle Book
author: Rudyard Kipling
summary: Story collection, 1894. The best-known stories follow Mowgli, a boy raised by wolves in the Indian jungle and taught the Law of the Jungle by Baloo the bear and Bagheera the panther, with help from Kaa the python. Hunted by the tiger Shere Khan, Mowgli finally kills him in a buffalo stampede. Other stories include Rikki-Tikki-Tavi, a mongoose who saves an English family from cobras, and The White Seal.

title: The Call of the Wild
author: Jack London
summary: Novel, 1903. Buck, a big St. Bernard and Scotch shepherd cross, is stolen from a California ranch and sold as a sled dog in the Klondike gold rush. He learns the 'law of club and fang', kills the lead dog Spitz and takes his place. After inexperienced owners drive the team onto river ice and drown, Buck is saved by John Thornton, whom he comes to love. When the Yeehat people kill Thornton, Buck avenges him and joins a wolf pack, remembered as the Ghost Dog.

title: White Fang
author: Jack London
summary: Novel, 1906. White Fang, part wolf and part dog, is born in the wild of the Yukon, raised in the camp of Grey Beaver, and sold to the cruel Beauty Smith, who makes him a fighting dog. Nearly killed by a bulldog, he is rescued by the mining engineer Weedon Scott, who tames him with patience. Taken to California, White Fang saves Scott's father, a judge, from the escaped convict Jim Hall, and recovers to live out his life with the family.

title: Heart of Darkness
author: Joseph Conrad
summary: Novella, 1899. On a boat in the Thames, Marlow tells of his journey up the Congo River as a steamboat captain for a Belgian trading company, witnessing the brutality of colonial rule. He is sent to bring back Kurtz, the company's most successful ivory agent, who has set himself up as a god among the local people, with heads on stakes around his hut. Kurtz dies on the boat going downriver, with the words 'The horror! The horror!' Back in Europe, Marlow tells Kurtz's fiancee that his last word was her name.

title: Robinson Crusoe
author: Daniel Defoe
summary: Novel, 1719. After a shipwreck, Crusoe spends twenty-eight years on an island near the mouth of the Orinoco. He salvages tools from the wreck, builds a fortified shelter, raises goats and grows grain, and keeps a journal. After finding a single footprint he discovers cannibals visiting the island and rescues one of their prisoners, whom he names Friday. When English mutineers land, Crusoe helps their captain retake the ship and finally sails home.

title: Gulliver's Travels
author: Jonathan Swift
summary: Satire, 1726. The ship's surgeon Lemuel Gulliver makes four voyages: to Lilliput, where six-inch people wage war over which end of an egg to break; to Brobdingnag, a land of giants who find human politics disgusting; to Laputa, a flying island of impractical scientists; and to the land of the Houyhnhnms, rational horses who rule the brutish, human-like Yahoos. He comes home so disgusted with humankind that he prefers the company of his horses.

title: The Scarlet Letter
author: Nathaniel Hawthorne
summary: Novel, 1850, set in Puritan Boston. Hester Prynne must wear a scarlet A for adultery after bearing a daughter, Pearl, and refuses to name the father, the respected young minister Arthur Dimmesdale. Her long-absent husband arrives under the name Roger Chillingworth and slowly torments Dimmesdale. Hester and Dimmesdale plan to flee, but he instead confesses on the public scaffold and dies in her arms. Chillingworth dies within a year and leaves his fortune to Pearl.

title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
author: Oscar Wilde
summary: Novel, 1890. The painter Basil Hallward paints the beautiful young Dorian Gray, and Lord Henry Wotton persuades him that only youth and pleasure matter. Dorian wishes the portrait would age instead of him, and it does, recording every sin while he stays young. He cruelly rejects the actress Sibyl Vane, who kills herself, lives a hidden life of vice, and murders Basil. Finally he stabs the portrait; the servants find an old, withered man dead on the floor and the portrait restored to its original beauty.

title: Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
summary: Novella, 1886. The London lawyer Utterson investigates the brutish Edward Hyde, who tramples a child and later murders Sir Danvers Carew, and who seems to have a hold over the respected Dr Henry Jekyll. When Jekyll's servants break into his laboratory they find Hyde dead by his own hand. Jekyll's written confession explains that he made a potion to separate his evil side, became Hyde at will, and at last began turning into Hyde without the drug and could not change back.

title: Kidnapped
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
summary: Novel, 1886, set in Scotland in 1751. Orphaned David Balfour goes to his miserly uncle Ebenezer, who tries to kill him and then has him kidnapped onto the brig Covenant to be sold in the Carolinas. On board David befriends the Jacobite Alan Breck Stewart. After a shipwreck, they are suspected in the Appin murder of Colin Campbell, the 'Red Fox', and flee across the Highlands. David returns, tricks his uncle into confessing, and claims his inheritance.

title: The Great Gatsby
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
summary: Novel, 1925, set on Long Island in 1922 and told by Nick Carraway. His neighbour, the mysterious millionaire Jay Gatsby, throws lavish parties hoping to win back Nick's cousin Daisy, now married to the brutish Tom Buchanan, who is having an affair with Myrtle Wilson. Driving Gatsby's car, Daisy hits and kills Myrtle; Gatsby takes the blame. Myrtle's husband George shoots Gatsby and then himself. Almost no one comes to the funeral, and Nick goes back west.

title: Hamlet
author: William Shakespeare
summary: Tragedy, about 1600. Prince Hamlet's father's ghost tells him that his uncle Claudius murdered him to take the throne and marry Hamlet's mother, Gertrude. Hamlet feigns madness, rejects Ophelia, and stages a play to catch Claudius's guilt. He kills Polonius, hidden behind a curtain; Ophelia goes mad and drowns. Her brother Laertes duels Hamlet with a poisoned sword; Gertrude drinks poisoned wine meant for Hamlet; Hamlet, fatally wounded, kills Claudius and dies. Fortinbras of Norway takes the throne, and Horatio lives to tell the story.

title: Macbeth
author: William Shakespeare
summary: Tragedy, about 1606. Three witches tell the Scottish general Macbeth he will be king. Urged on by Lady Macbeth, he murders King Duncan and takes the throne, then has his friend Banquo killed, though Banquo's son Fleance escapes, and slaughters Macduff's family. Lady Macbeth, haunted by guilt, sleepwalks and dies. Macbeth trusts the witches' promise that no man born of woman can harm him, but Birnam Wood comes to Dunsinane as soldiers carry its branches, and Macduff, 'untimely ripped' from his mother's womb, kills him. Duncan's son Malcolm becomes king.

title: Romeo and Juliet
author: William Shakespeare
summary: Tragedy, about 1595. In Verona, Romeo of the Montagues and Juliet of the rival Capulets fall in love and are secretly married by Friar Laurence. After Juliet's cousin Tybalt kills Romeo's friend Mercutio, Romeo kills Tybalt and is banished. To escape a forced marriage to Paris, Juliet takes a potion that makes her seem dead, but the friar's message never reaches Romeo. He finds her in the tomb, poisons himself, and she wakes, finds him dead and stabs herself. The two families are reconciled over their bodies.

title: The Odyssey
author: Homer
summary: Greek epic poem. After the Trojan War, Odysseus takes ten years to reach his home on Ithaca. He blinds the Cyclops Polyphemus, angering the sea god Poseidon; escapes the witch Circe, visits the underworld, sails past the Sirens and between Scylla and Charybdis, and is held for seven years by the nymph Calypso. The Phaeacians carry him home, where he arrives disguised as a beggar. His wife Penelope has held off a crowd of suitors; Odysseus wins the contest of stringing his great bow, kills the suitors with his son Telemachus, and is reunited with Penelope.

title: The Iliad
author: Homer
summary: Greek epic poem, set in the tenth year of the Trojan War. Achilles quarrels with Agamemnon over the captive woman Briseis and withdraws from the fighting, and the Trojans under Hector drive the Greeks back to their ships. Achilles' friend Patroclus fights in his armour and is killed by Hector. Achilles returns, kills Hector and drags his body behind his chariot. King Priam comes secretly to Achilles' tent to ransom his son's body, and the poem ends with Hector's funeral. It does not tell the wooden horse or the fall of Troy.

title: Emma
author: Jane Austen
summary: Novel, 1815. Emma Woodhouse, rich, clever and sure of herself, plays matchmaker in the village of Highbury. She persuades her friend Harriet Smith to refuse the farmer Robert Martin in hopes of the vicar Mr Elton, who wants Emma instead. Frank Churchill flirts with Emma while secretly engaged to Jane Fairfax. After Emma insults poor Miss Bates at a Box Hill picnic and is scolded by her old friend Mr Knightley, she realises she loves him. They marry, and Harriet marries Robert Martin after all.

title: Persuasion
author: Jane Austen
summary: Novel, 1817. Eight years earlier Anne Elliot was persuaded by her friend Lady Russell to break off her engagement to the penniless naval officer Frederick Wentworth. He returns a rich captain and seems to court Louisa Musgrove, until Louisa is badly hurt jumping from the sea wall at Lyme. In Bath, Anne's cousin Mr Elliot courts her but is exposed as a schemer. Wentworth writes Anne a letter, 'You pierce my soul', and they marry.

title: Sense and Sensibility
author: Jane Austen
summary: Novel, 1811. After their father's death the Dashwood sisters, sensible Elinor and passionate Marianne, move to a Devon cottage with their mother. Elinor loves Edward Ferrars, who is secretly engaged to the scheming Lucy Steele. Marianne is swept away by the dashing Willoughby, who abandons her to marry money; heartbroken, she falls dangerously ill. Lucy marries Edward's brother Robert instead, Edward marries Elinor, and Marianne comes to love the steady Colonel Brandon.

title: The Scarlet Pimpernel
author: Baroness Orczy
summary: Novel, 1905. In 1792 a secret band of Englishmen led by the mysterious Scarlet Pimpernel smuggles French aristocrats out of revolutionary France. The French agent Chauvelin blackmails Marguerite Blakeney, whose brother he holds, into helping unmask the Pimpernel. She discovers that the leader is her own husband, Sir Percy, who plays a foolish dandy in public, and races to France to warn him. Percy outwits Chauvelin in disguise and escapes with Marguerite and the rescued refugees.

title: Black Beauty
author: Anna Sewell
summary: Novel, 1877, told by the horse himself. Black Beauty grows up at Birtwick Park with the kind Gordons and his friends Ginger and Merrylegs. Sold on after an accident, he suffers the cruel bearing rein, bad grooms and careless owners, then works as a London cab horse for the good Jerry Barker. He sees Ginger worn out and dead. At last he is bought by kind ladies in the country, where his old stable boy Joe Green recognises him, and he ends his days in peace.

title: The Phantom of the Opera
author: Gaston Leroux
summary: Novel, 1910. The Paris Opera is haunted by the Phantom, Erik, a disfigured genius who lives in its cellars beside an underground lake. He secretly trains the young singer Christine Daae, who thinks him the Angel of Music. When she falls in love with her childhood friend Raoul de Chagny, Erik drops the great chandelier and carries her to his lair. Moved when Christine kisses his forehead, he lets her go with Raoul, and dies soon after.

title: Ethan Frome
author: Edith Wharton
summary: Novella, 1911, set in wintry Starkfield, Massachusetts. The poor farmer Ethan Frome is trapped in a bleak marriage to his sickly, complaining wife Zeena and falls in love with her young cousin Mattie Silver, who helps in the house. When Zeena sends Mattie away, Ethan and Mattie try to kill themselves by sledding into an elm tree. Both survive, crippled, and spend their lives in the farmhouse with Zeena caring for Mattie.

title: The Invisible Man
author: H. G. Wells
summary: Novel, 1897. A bandaged stranger takes a room at an inn in Iping; he is Griffin, a scientist who has made himself invisible and cannot reverse it. Exposed, he turns to theft and violence and seeks refuge with his old acquaintance Dr Kemp, to whom he tells his story and his plan for a reign of terror. Kemp betrays him to the police, and Griffin is beaten to death by a crowd, his body slowly becoming visible.

title: The Metamorphosis
author: Franz Kafka
summary: Novella, 1915. Gregor Samsa, a travelling salesman who supports his family, wakes to find himself turned into a giant insect. His family is horrified; his sister Grete feeds him at first, his father wounds him with an apple that lodges in his back. As the family takes in lodgers and goes to work, they come to see him as a burden. Gregor dies alone, and the relieved family takes a trip to the country, making plans for Grete's future.

title: Beowulf
author: Anonymous (Old English)
summary: Old English epic poem. The Geatish hero Beowulf comes to the aid of the Danish king Hrothgar, whose hall Heorot is attacked each night by the monster Grendel, and tears off Grendel's arm. He then kills Grendel's vengeful mother in her lair beneath a lake. Beowulf rules the Geats for fifty years; in old age he fights a dragon that is ravaging the land and kills it with the help of young Wiglaf, but dies of his wounds and is burned on a funeral pyre.

title: Walden
author: Henry David Thoreau
summary: Nonfiction, 1854. Thoreau describes the two years and two months, from 1845 to 1847, that he lived in a small cabin he built himself on the shore of Walden Pond near Concord, Massachusetts. He sets out the economy of a simple life, what he spent and grew, and argues for self-reliance and living deliberately. Chapters follow the seasons, his bean field, visitors, the animals and the pond itself, and end with the spring thaw.

title: Meditations
author: Marcus Aurelius
summary: Private notebooks written in Greek by the Roman emperor Marcus Aurelius, probably between 170 and 180 AD while on campaign, never meant for publication. They are Stoic reminders to himself: that we control our judgements but not events, to do one's duty to others without complaint, that everything changes and passes, and that death is a natural dissolution, like birth, not to be feared.

title: Paradise Lost
author: John Milton
summary: Epic poem, 1667. Satan and the rebel angels, defeated in their war against God, wake in Hell and build Pandemonium. Satan travels to Eden and, in the form of a serpent, tempts Eve to eat from the Tree of Knowledge; Adam eats too, out of love for her. The angel Michael shows Adam the future of humankind, including redemption, and the poem ends with Adam and Eve leaving Paradise hand in hand.

title: Siddhartha
author: Hermann Hesse
summary: Novel, 1922. Siddhartha, a Brahmin's son in ancient India, leaves home with his friend Govinda to live as a wandering ascetic. He meets the Buddha, Gotama, but decides he must find his own way. He then lives a worldly life with the courtesan Kamala and the merchant Kamaswami until disgust drives him to the river. There he becomes a ferryman with the wise Vasudeva, loses the son he had with Kamala, and finds enlightenment by listening to the river.

title: Tarzan of the Apes
author: Edgar Rice Burroughs
summary: Novel, 1912. John and Alice Clayton, Lord and Lady Greystoke, are marooned on the African coast and die there; their baby is raised by the she-ape Kala and named Tarzan. He teaches himself to read from his parents' books and becomes lord of the apes. He saves the American Jane Porter and falls in love with her. He learns he is the rightful Lord Greystoke, but Jane is engaged to his cousin William Clayton, who holds the title, and Tarzan keeps his parentage secret so that she will be provided for.

title: A Princess of Mars
author: Edgar Rice Burroughs
summary: Novel, 1912 in magazine form, 1917 as a book. John Carter, a Confederate veteran prospecting in Arizona, is mysteriously transported to Mars, called Barsoom. Captured by the green Tharks, he wins their respect and the friendship of Tars Tarkas, and rescues Dejah Thoris, princess of Helium, whom he marries. When the planet's atmosphere plant fails, he forces it open to save Mars, loses consciousness, and wakes back on Earth.

title: The Thirty-Nine Steps
author: John Buchan
summary: Novel, 1915. In London in 1914, Richard Hannay's upstairs neighbour Franklin Scudder is murdered after telling him of a German plot. Hunted by the police and the spies, Hannay flees across the Scottish moors, decoding Scudder's notebook. The 'thirty-nine steps' lead down to the sea at a house on the Kent coast, where Hannay and the authorities catch the spy ring, the Black Stone, before they can leave with British naval plans.
